titulo: Imperfect subjunctive: How the imperfect subjunctive is formed

aula.objetivo: Form the imperfecto de subjuntivo (-ra and -se, regular and irregular) from the pretérito indefinido, use it when the main verb is in the past («Quería que vinieras»), with «ojalá», «como si» and in polite requests («quisiera»), and with «para que», «antes de que», «sin que» and relative clauses.

sessao.titulo: How the imperfect subjunctive is formed

blocos.titulo: From the indefinido to the imperfecto de subjuntivo
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the «imperfecto de subjuntivo» is the past subjunctive. You use it when the main verb is in the past and calls for the subjunctive: «Quiero que vengas» (I want you to come) becomes «Quería que vinieras» (I wanted you to come). English keeps "you to come" in both; Spanish shifts the subjunctive to the past. STEP 2: English has one survivor of this form: "WERE" in "If I were you", "I wish it were Friday", "as if he were the boss". Spanish «fuera» is exactly that "were" — and Spanish has it for every verb. STEP 3: to form it, start from the «ellos» form of the pretérito indefinido: «hablaron», «comieron», «vivieron». STEP 4: drop the final «-ron»: «habla-», «comie-», «vivie-». STEP 5: add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -rais, -ran: «hablara, hablaras, hablara, habláramos, hablarais, hablaran». Only the «nosotros» form has a written accent, on the vowel before the ending: «habláramos», «comiéramos», «viviéramos». STEP 6: irregular verbs have no new rule. The stem comes from the indefinido: «tuvieron» gives «tuviera», «fueron» gives «fuera», «dijeron» gives «dijera». If you know the «ellos» indefinido, you know this form. STEP 7: there's a second set, in -se: «hablase, hablases, hablase, hablásemos, hablaseis, hablasen». The meaning is the same. In Spain both are used (-ra more in speech); in Latin America -ra dominates. In this lesson the sentences use -ra, and the tables show both. STEP 8: one form covers «yo» and «él»: «Quería que yo tuviera» and «Quería que él tuviera». Use the pronoun when you need to make clear who does it.
blocos.comparacao: You know one past subjunctive form already: English "were" in "If I WERE you", "I wish it WERE Friday". Spanish has one for every verb, built from the «ellos» indefinido minus «-ron» plus «-ra»: tuvieron → tuviera, fueron → fuera. And "I wanted you to come" = «Quería que vinieras».

exemplos.ru: Quería que vinieras a mi casa.
exemplos.pt: I wanted you to come to my place.

exemplos.ru: Mis padres querían que estudiara medicina.
exemplos.pt: My parents wanted me to study medicine.

exemplos.ru: Era importante que dijeras la verdad.
exemplos.pt: It was important for you to tell the truth.

tabelas.titulo: Regular verbs (the -ra set, with the -se set alongside)
Irregular verbs: the stem comes from the «ellos» indefinido

erros.motivo: A main verb in the past calls for the imperfecto de subjuntivo, not the present.
After «pedir que» comes the subjunctive, and the «nosotros» form has an accent.
The stem is that of the indefinido «vinieron», with «-ie-».
«Dudar que» takes the subjunctive; «tenía» would be indicative.

blocos.enunciado: Say out loud what people wanted from you when you were a child, with «mis padres querían que…», «mi profesor quería que…», «mis amigos querían que…». Use at least one irregular verb.

Say out loud five sentences with the present subjunctive: «Quiero que vengas», «Espero que tengas tiempo»… Then conjugate the pretérito indefinido of «tener», «ir» and «decir» in the «ellos» form: tuvieron, fueron, dijeron.
